exposure: Acute kidney injury (AKI) treated with dialysis during pregnancy or within 12 weeks of delivery
outcome: Incidence of AKI treated with dialysis
Major pregnancy-related complications (preeclampsia, thrombotic microangiopathy, heart failure, sepsis, postpartum hemorrhage)
cohort: The study included 1,918,789 consecutive pregnancies in Ontario, Canada, over a 15-year period (1997-2011), with 188 cases complicated by AKI treated with dialysis.
finding: AKI treated with dialysis during pregnancy is rare, typically occurring in healthy women who acquire a major pregnancy-related medical condition like preeclampsia, and many affected women and their babies have good short-term outcomes.
birth_weight: Low birth weight (<2500 g) was an observed outcome in affected pregnancies.
gest_age: Preterm birth (<37 weeks' gestation) was an observed outcome in affected pregnancies.
